Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 20, verse 134:

Allah's words ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment﴾ to the end of the verse form a resumptive sentence (jumlah mustaanifah) that confirms what precedes it, namely that the Qur'an is a clear sign that cannot be denied, by showing that they will acknowledge it on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning is: And if We had destroyed them in this world with a punishment that uproots them ﴿before it﴾. The phrase ﴿before it﴾ is connected either to "We destroyed" or to something omitted that serves as an adjective for "punishment", meaning: a punishment that occurred before it. The pronoun refers either to the clear proof (al-bayyinah), and the masculine form is used because it is understood as a proof and evidence, or to the coming (al-ityan) implied by the verb, meaning: before the coming of the clear proof. Abu Hayyan said that the pronoun refers to the Messenger, based on the context of what follows the mention of the Messenger. This is also the view of the one who said: that is, before the sending of Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) (ﷺ). ﴿They would have said﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger﴾ in the world ﴿with signs﴾, ﴿so that we might follow Your signs﴾ which he brought to us ﴿before we were humiliated﴾ by the punishment in this world ﴿and disgraced﴾ by entering the Fire today. Abu Hayyan said: humiliation (dhull) and disgrace (khizy) both refer to the punishment of the Hereafter. He related the interpretation of dhull as abasement (hawan) and of khizy as exposure (iftidah). The meaning is that if We had destroyed them before this, they would have said: "Why did You not send us a messenger, and we would not have been destroyed before it?" Thus their excuse is cut off. At that point ﴿they will say: Yes, indeed a warner came to us, but we denied and said: Allah has revealed nothing﴾.

Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, Zayd ibn Ali, al-Hasan (in the narration of Abbad), al-Umari, Dawud, al-Fazari, Abu Hatim and Ya'qub read ﴿we are humiliated and disgraced﴾ (nudhall wa-nakhza) in the passive voice.

The Ash'aris (the Ash'ari school of theology) used the verse as evidence that obligation (wujub) is established only through the revealed law (shar'). Al-Jubba'i (the Mu'tazili theologian) used it as evidence for the obligation of lutf (divine grace or favour, the view that God must do what is best for His servants) upon Allah, exalted and majestic is He. However, this is open to question.

**Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 20, verse 135 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿Say﴾ to those rebellious disbelievers, ﴿each﴾ means each one of us and of you, ﴿is waiting﴾, that is, awaiting what our affair and your affair will come to. It is the predicate of ﴿each﴾. Its singular form is due to treating it grammatically according to its wording: ﴿so wait﴾. It is also read as "so enjoy" (fa-tamatta'u), and "so you will know" (fa-sa-ta'lamuna) soon ﴿who are the companions of the even path﴾, that is, the straight one. Abu Mijlaz and Imran ibn Hudayr read "al-sawa'" (the even), meaning the middle, and what is intended by it is the good.

Al-Jahdari and Ibn Ya'mur read "al-su'a" with a damma and without the madd, on the pattern of fu'la. It is the feminine of al-asw'a (the worst), and it is made feminine because al-sirat (the path) is feminine, though the word is used both as masculine and feminine. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, read "al-saw'" with a fatha, a sukun, and a hamza at its end, meaning evil. It is also read "al-suwayy" with a damma on the sin, a fatha on the waw, and a shadda on the ya'. This is the diminutive of sau' with a fatha. It was also said to be the diminutive of su' with a damma. Abu Hayyan said: "The better view is that it is the diminutive of sawa', as they say of 'ata', 'utayy, because if it were the diminutive of that, its hamza would remain." It was also said: "suwi'i," and this was criticised on the grounds that replacing such a hamza with ya' is permissible. It is also reported from al-Jahdari and Ibn Ya'mur that they read "al-suwa" with a damma, a short vowel, and a shadda on the waw. In explaining this reading, it is preferred that its origin is al-su'a, as in the first narration: the hamza was lightened by replacing it with a waw, and the waw was assimilated into the following waw. The contrast between what precedes and the words of Allah, ﴿and whoever is guided﴾, that is, from misguidance, has been observed in most of these readings, but it is not observed in the reading of the majority. The first is among the irregular readings.

The word "man" in both places is interrogative, in a position of raising (nasb/raf') as the subject (mubtada'), and the predicate is what follows after the conjunction, which is a conjunction of sentences. The two conjoined sentences together take the place of the two objects of "knowing," or its single object if it means "knowing" in the sense of recognition. It is permitted that the second "man" be a relative pronoun, so that it is conjoined to the position of the first interrogative sentence, whose verb is suspended, on the basis that "knowing" here means recognition, which takes one object. Otherwise the relative pronoun, through the conjunction, would be one of the two objects, and the other object would have to be omitted for brevity, which is not permitted.

It is also permitted that it be conjoined to "companions" (ashab), so that it falls within the scope of the interrogative "man," meaning: "and who is the one who was guided." Or it may be conjoined to "the path," so that it falls within the scope of "companions," meaning: "and who are the companions of the one who was guided," that is, the Prophet (ﷺ). If by "the even path" the Prophet (peace be upon him) is also meant, then the conjunction is one of attributes conjoined to attributes, while the essence is one.

Al-Farra' permitted that the first "man" also be a relative pronoun, meaning "those who." It is in the position of accusative (nasb) as the object of "knowing" in the sense of recognition. "Companions" is the predicate of an omitted subject, which is the returning pronoun, meaning: "those who are the companions of the path." This is permissible according to the doctrine of the Kufans, who permit omitting such a returning pronoun whether or not the relative clause is long, and whether the relative pronoun is "ayy" or another. The Basrans disagree. How closely this conclusion matches the opening of the Surah (al-Fatiha) is striking. Al-Tibi mentioned that it is a noble conclusion, looking back to al-Fatiha, and that when it becomes clear that the Qur'an was sent down to bear the hardship of conveying the message, "Do not wear yourself out": once you have conveyed and exerted your effort, there is no blame upon you. Devote yourself to obedience to Him as far as your capacity allows. Command your family, who are your community that follows you, to do the same. Leave aside those for whom warning is of no benefit, for it is a reminder only to the one who fears, and the opponent will regret when regret no longer benefits him. End of quotation.

* * *

**(And from the allusive interpretation (ishara, a mystical or esoteric reading) of the verses)** ﴿Then Moses sensed fear within himself﴾. It was said: he, peace be upon him, saw that Allah had clothed the magic of the magicians in the garment of domination, so he feared the domination, for none feels secure from the plotting of Allah except the people who are lost.

[p. 288]

Ibn 'Ata' was asked about this and said: "He, peace be upon him, did not fear for himself. He feared for his people, that they would miss their share from Allah, the Exalted." ﴿We said: Do not fear; indeed you are the highest﴾, that is: indeed you are the one guarded by the eyes of care and the guard of gentleness. Or: you are the one of high rank, who prevails over them with complete dominance, such that by it they become among your followers, so their share from Allah, the Exalted, will not be lost. ﴿Then the magicians were thrown down prostrate﴾, to the end of what happened with them. In this is an allusion that Allah, the Exalted, bestows favour on whomever He wills with success and with arrival at Him, glorified be He, in the shortest time. So it is not unlikely that perfection is attained by one who repents and travels under the hand of a perfect mentor in a short period. Many ignorant people deny to the wayfarers (salikin) who repent, when they are recently departed from sins and freed from defects, that they attain perfection and that goodness overflows upon them. They say: "How can this come to them, when yesterday they were such and such?" Their statement, ﴿They said: We will never prefer you﴾, and so on, is a speech issuing from the greatness of resolve that arises in the soul through the strength of certainty. For when this is attained by the soul, it does not care for worldly happiness, bodily misery, transient pleasures, or sensory pains, in comparison with the happiness of the Hereafter and the enduring spiritual delight.

﴿And We revealed to Moses: Travel by night with My servants﴾, and so on. In this there is an allusion to the recommendation of withdrawing from strangers and abandoning the company of the wicked. ﴿And do not transgress therein﴾: he counted as transgression therein the use of it while heedless of Allah, and not intending to protect oneself by it against His fear, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And what hastened you away from your people, O Moses?﴾ The allusion in this is that it is fitting for a leader to observe what is best for those under him, and for a shaykh not to do what might cause the disciple (murid) to think badly, especially when the disciple has no firm footing at all. ﴿He said: We have indeed tried your people after you﴾.

Ibn 'Ata' said: Allah, the Exalted, said to Moses, peace be upon him, after informing him of this: "Do you know from where you were tested?" He said: "No, my Lord." He, glorified be He, said: "From your saying to Aaron: 'Take my place among my people,' and from not entrusting the matter to Me, and from relying upon Me in the succession."

Some have mentioned that the secret of Allah, the Exalted, informing him of what was mentioned is His intimacy with him, peace be upon him, and his being occupied with His company rather than with the company of opposites. But this is as you see.

﴿And the Samiri misled them﴾: he became the cause of their misguidance through what he made. Some of the people of interpretation (ta'wil) said: Allah, the Exalted, tested them with what He tested them with, so that there might be distinguished from them the one prepared and receptive to perfection through abstraction, from the one of weak preparedness, immersed in matter, who perceives only the sensible and does not awaken to the purely intelligible. For this reason they said: ﴿We did not break our promise to you by our own power﴾, that is, by our own opinion. For they were slaves by nature, having no opinion of their own, no faculty, and not free; they had no way except imitation and action, not verification and knowledge. The Samiri enslaved them through a talisman made from the stripped jewelry, because the love of gold was firmly rooted in their souls. For it is lower and drawn toward corporeal nature, and it adorns the golden nature and beautifies that specific form within it, because of natural affinity. This was by way of mixing the heavenly powers, which are the effect of the universal animal soul of the heavens, alluded to by "Haizum," and the horse of life, which is the vehicle of Gabriel, peace be upon him, indicating the active intellect, with the earthly powers. For this reason he said: ﴿I perceived what they did not perceive﴾, that is, of natural and mathematical knowledge, upon which the science of talismans and magic is based. ﴿He said: Go, for it is yours in this life to say: "No touching"﴾. He, peace be upon him, said this in anger at the Samiri and to banish him. Everyone against whom the prophets, and likewise the saints, become angry, because they are manifestations of the attributes of the Real, the Exalted, falls under His domination, and is wretched in this world and the Hereafter. The form of the punishment of this outcast, in avoiding contact, was a consequence of his remoteness from the Truth in calling to falsehood, and an effect of Moses' curse upon him, peace be upon him, when his plot was voided and his deception removed.

﴿And they ask you about the mountains; say: My Lord will blow them away with a blowing﴾. The People of Unity (ahl al-wahda) said: That is, they ask you about the existences of things. Say: My Lord will blow them away by the winds of divine breaths arising from the mine of Oneness, and will scatter them on the Great Resurrection as a level plain, a single existence. ﴿You will see in it no crookedness or curve﴾, no duality and no otherness. ﴿On that day they will follow the Caller﴾

[p. 289]

who is the Truth, glorified be He, having no crookedness, since He, the Exalted, takes hold of their forelocks, and He is upon a straight path. ﴿And voices will be humbled before the Most Merciful﴾, since no act belongs to anyone other than Him, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿So you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾, a hidden matter, with respect to its attribution to the manifestations. End of quotation.

How many such interpretations they have! And Allah, the Exalted, is the Protector. ﴿On that day intercession will not benefit, except for one whom the Most Merciful permits and whose word He approves﴾. It was said: this is the one whose action and belief are sound, who attributes nothing to himself and sees no action of his own.

﴿And they cannot encompass Him in knowledge﴾ because of the perfection of His holiness, His transcendence, and His majesty, glorified be He, the Mighty and Majestic. So far is it that the gnat of thought could fly into the atmosphere of the heaven of sovereignty, or that the bee of the rational soul could graze upon the flowers of the gardens of the wilderness of divinity (lahut). Yes, creatures differ in knowledge of His attributes, the Mighty and Majestic, according to the difference of their readiness. This is the knowledge indicated by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge﴾. It was also said: this is an allusion to the knowledge bestowed directly (ilm ladunni, knowledge from the presence of God). The allusion in the story of Adam, peace be upon him, is that a person should exercise greater caution against falling into disobedience. How well did the one who said:

O you who look with the eye of a sleeper, and witness the matter without witnessing it,
You have deluded your soul into error, and it refused the paths of hope, which are not leading ones.
You join sin to sin and hope for the stations of the Gardens through them, and the winning of the worshipper.
You forgot that Allah expelled Adam from them to this world because of one sin.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: While Adam, peace be upon him, was weeping, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him, and Adam wept, and Gabriel wept at his weeping, peace be upon them both. He said: "O Adam, what is this weeping?" He said: "O Gabriel, how can I not weep, when my Lord has moved me from the heaven to the earth, and from the house of blessing to the house of misery?" Gabriel, peace be upon him, carried Adam's words, and Allah, the Exalted, said: "O Gabriel, go to him and say to him: 'O Adam, your Lord says to you: Did I not create you with My own hand? Did I not breathe into you of My spirit? Did I not make My angels prostrate to you? Did I not settle you in My Garden? Did I not command you, and you disobeyed Me? By My might and My majesty, if all the earth were filled with men like you, then disobeyed Me, I would surely send them down to the abodes of the disobedient. Yet, O Adam, My mercy has preceded My wrath. I have heard your supplication, I have had mercy on your weeping, and I have pardoned your slip.'"

﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾, that is, by turning toward the lower world, ﴿indeed for him is a straitened life﴾ because of the dominance of his avarice and the severity of his stinginess. For the one who turns away from the threshold of the Truth, glorified be He, has his soul drawn to worldly adornments and material possessions, because of their affinity with him. His greed and craving for them increase, and his passion for them grows, because of kinship, sharing in darkness, and inclination toward the lower direction. So he withholds them from himself and from others. And whenever he acquires more of them, his greed for them and his stinginess with them increase. That is the straitened life.

Therefore some have said: No one turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, glorified is He, except that his time becomes dark for him and his provision is disturbed for him. By contrast, the one who remembers and turns toward Him, exalted is He, has certainty in Him, mighty and majestic is He, and reliance upon Him, exalted is He, is in ease of life and abundance. He spends what he finds, and he is content with his Lord, glorified is He, regarding what he lacks.

﴿And the good end is for the people of taqwa﴾. That is: the good end which is worthy of being considered and deserving of being called an end for the people of taqwa (God-consciousness), those who are free of the vices of the soul and adorned with the virtues of the spirit. We ask God, exalted is He, to bestow upon us a good end and a life purified from turmoil. We praise Him, glorified is He, for His bounties, and we send blessings and peace upon the best of His prophets and upon his family, the best of families, as long as a star rises and a light shines.

The sixteenth part is complete. Following it, God willing, is the seventeenth part, and its beginning is Surat al-Anbiya'.
